It uses text embeddings to interpret the meaning of the text and generate matching emphasis, pauses, and tone, and Amazon says the result is a voice that differentiates dialogue from narration and mimics elements such as surprise. disadvantages: Available in only two languages, English (US) and Spanish (Spain), with six voices total.
Available only in the US East (N. Virginia) AWS region, per Amazon's region list.

Amazon warns that updates to the model's training data can cause slight variations in how a voice sounds over time, which can affect projects synthesized in parts over a long period, such as a season of podcasts.

aws_polly/neural.description: Amazon Polly's Neural engine (NTTS) is one of four text-to-speech voice engines Polly offers, alongside Standard, Long-form, and Generative. Instead of concatenating recorded speech fragments like the Standard engine, it uses a sequence-to-sequence neural network to turn phonemes into spectrograms and a neural vocoder to render them as audio, producing more natural prosody, stress, and intonation. It is available across 36 languages and language variants, several with multiple named male and female voices.
disadvantages: Not available in all AWS Regions; supported in only 19 Regions, fewer than Standard voices.
For certain voices, Polly can automatically switch to the Standard engine when accuracy is critical, such as letter-by-letter spelling, producing an audible shift in voice quality.

Amazon Polly's newer Generative engine, described by AWS as its largest TTS model to date, produces more emotionally engaged, human-like speech than Neural for the subset of voices and regions it supports.

aws_polly/standard.description: Amazon Polly Standard is the original text-to-speech engine in AWS's Amazon Polly service, using concatenative synthesis that joins phonemes of recorded human speech into audio. It is one of four Polly voice engines, alongside Neural, Long-Form and Generative, which AWS documents as producing more natural, human-like speech than Standard. AWS currently offers 60 Standard voices (40 female, 20 male) across 29 languages and language variants, each usable for real-time or asynchronous synthesis with SSML markup and Polly speech marks.
disadvantages: AWS says concatenative synthesis has an inherent ceiling: 'the inevitable variations in speech and the techniques used to segment the waveforms limits the quality of speech' compared with its Neural, Long-Form and Generative engines.

aws_transcribe/StartTranscriptionJob.description: StartTranscriptionJob is the Amazon Transcribe API operation that runs an asynchronous (batch) speech-to-text job: given a media file already uploaded to Amazon S3, it returns a text transcript, optionally with speaker diarization, custom-vocabulary support, PII redaction, toxic-speech detection, and subtitle output. Amazon Transcribe is AWS's fully managed automatic speech recognition service, which AWS describes as powered by a next-generation, multi-billion-parameter speech foundation model trained on millions of hours of audio. This operation covers Transcribe's batch mode only; real-time audio uses a separate streaming API.
disadvantages: StartTranscriptionJob only transcribes media already uploaded to Amazon S3; real-time audio requires Amazon Transcribe's separate streaming API.
AWS's API reference and documentation for this operation publish no accuracy (word error rate) figures.

azure/eu/text-embedding-3-large.description: text-embedding-3-large is OpenAI's largest and most capable text embedding model, producing embeddings of up to 3,072 dimensions from text input, useful for semantic search, clustering, recommendations, anomaly detection, and classification. It is part of OpenAI's third-generation embedding family (alongside the smaller text-embedding-3-small) and supersedes text-embedding-ada-002. It supports a `dimensions` parameter (Matryoshka-style representation learning) that lets the output embedding be shortened for lower storage and compute cost with only a modest quality loss. On Azure, it is offered as a Foundry model sold directly by Microsoft for use with the Embeddings API.
disadvantages: Can only be used with Embedding API requests, not general chat or completion endpoints, per OpenAI's model documentation.

disadvantages: Shut down by OpenAI on March 26, 2026, per OpenAI's deprecations page, which recommends gpt-5 or gpt-4.1 as replacements.

azure/us/text-embedding-3-large.description: text-embedding-3-large is OpenAI's largest and most capable text embedding model, producing embeddings of up to 3,072 dimensions from text input, useful for semantic search, clustering, recommendations, anomaly detection, and classification. Anthropic's own model page says to start with Claude Opus 5 for most workloads and reach for Fable 5.1 only when evaluations at higher effort still fall short; an invitation-only sibling, Claude Mythos 5.1, offers the same capabilities with more permissive safeguards for vetted cybersecurity and biology-research partners.
disadvantages: Three changes from Claude Fable 5 are breaking: forced tool use returns an error, earlier models can't read its thinking blocks, and editing earlier turns invalidates thinking blocks, per Anthropic's release notes.

It is a 671-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with about 37 billion parameters active per token, released January 20, 2025 under the MIT license. AWS offers it as a fully managed, serverless model on Amazon Bedrock with a 128K-token context window. DeepSeek's own website now lists R1 only in its research/model history section behind the newer V3, V3.1, V3.2, V4 and V4.1 families, and DeepSeek's current API pricing page no longer lists an R1/deepseek-reasoner endpoint among its current models.
disadvantages: Superseded within DeepSeek's own model lineup by the V3, V3.1, V3.2, V4 and V4.1 families, and no longer listed as a current model on DeepSeek's own API pricing page (deepseek.com; api-docs.deepseek.com).
Knowledge cutoff of January 2025, per AWS's Bedrock model card.
Text-only: no image, audio or video input or output support (AWS Bedrock model card).

bedrock/global.openai.gpt-6-luna.description: GPT-6 Luna is OpenAI's fast, cost-efficient model in the GPT-6 family, released September 22, 2026 alongside GPT-6 Sol as the successor to GPT-5.6 Luna. AWS's Bedrock blog describes it as built for high-frequency, repeatable tasks such as extracting information from large document collections, summarizing incoming material, classifying inputs and answering focused questions. It takes text and image input and produces text output, with a knowledge cutoff of May 18, 2026 and reasoning effort adjustable per request from none up to max.
disadvantages: Output is text-only; the model does not generate images, audio or video.
Not compatible with Live sessions, Realtime, Assistants, fine-tuning, embeddings, or audio/video features.
Knowledge cutoff of May 18, 2026.
Artificial Analysis measured a time-to-first-token of about 109 seconds at max reasoning effort, well above the roughly 2-second median for comparable reasoning models.
AWS positions Luna below GPT-6 Sol in capability, intended for high-volume, repeatable tasks rather than the complex, multistep reasoning work Sol handles.

bedrock/global.twelvelabs.pegasus-1-2-v1.description: Pegasus v1.2 is TwelveLabs' video-to-text generation model, offered on Amazon Bedrock since February 2025, that takes a video (supplied as a storage location) together with a text prompt and produces descriptions, summaries, or answers about the video's content. It uses an encoder-decoder architecture combining a video encoder, tokenizer, and large language model, and TwelveLabs documents it as handling videos up to one hour long with temporal grounding that can localize events by timestamp. TwelveLabs' current product documentation centers on the newer Pegasus 1.5, which extends 1.2 with features such as video segmentation, video clipping, and a larger context and response window, indicating Pegasus v1.2 is an earlier generation of the model that remains available through Bedrock.
disadvantages: TwelveLabs' current documentation centers on the newer Pegasus 1.5, which adds video segmentation, video clipping, reference-image prompting, and a larger context and response window not documented for Pegasus v1.2.
Output is text only; it does not generate or edit video, image, or audio content.
On Amazon Bedrock it is only reachable through the Invoke API, without support for the Converse or Chat Completions APIs (Amazon Bedrock model card).

bedrock/jp.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7.description: Claude Opus 4.7 is Anthropic's most capable Opus model at its April 16, 2026 general-availability release, built for advanced, long-running software engineering and high-resolution image understanding. It is the first Claude model with high-resolution vision, accepting images up to about 3.75 megapixels versus roughly 1.15 megapixels on prior Claude models, and it adds a new 'xhigh' effort level between 'high' and 'max' for finer control over the reasoning-versus-latency trade-off. Anthropic ships it with safeguards that automatically detect and block high-risk cybersecurity requests, as part of a staged approach toward broader release of its more capable, access-restricted Mythos-class models.
disadvantages: Anthropic states it is less broadly capable than the access-restricted Claude Mythos Preview model (Anthropic launch post).
Anthropic states it is 'modestly weaker' than its predecessor on harm-reduction advice about controlled substances (Anthropic launch post).
Instruction-following changes mean prompts tuned for earlier Claude models can now produce unexpected results (Anthropic launch post).
Superseded within Anthropic's own Opus line by Opus 4.8, Opus 5 and Opus 5.5, all released within six months of Opus 4.7's launch (Anthropic model deprecations page).

bedrock/meta_llama_models.description: Llama 3.3 70B is a text-only instruction-tuned model developed by Meta, available on AWS Bedrock. It features 70 billion parameters and a 128,000-token context window, offering enhanced performance compared to Llama 3.1 70B while using fewer computational resources. The model excels in advanced reasoning, code generation, and multilingual tasks, making it ideal for enterprise applications requiring high performance and efficient resource utilization.
disadvantages: Text-only model with no multimodal capabilities (image/audio processing)
70B parameter size requires significant computational resources for deployment
Limited to AWS Bedrock infrastructure, restricting flexibility for non-AWS environments
Not suitable for resource-constrained or edge computing scenarios
No explicit benchmark scores provided for performance validation

bedrock/minimax.minimax-m2.description: MiniMax-M2 is a text-only Mixture-of-Experts language model from MiniMax, released October 27, 2025, built for coding and long-horizon agentic tool-use workflows. It has 230 billion total parameters with only 10 billion activated per token, an architecture aimed at fast, cost-efficient inference while running shell, browser, retrieval, and code-execution tool chains. It supports function calling and multi-step tool orchestration. MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.1, M2.5, M2.7, and M3) that supersede it in its own lineup.
disadvantages: Text-only model that does not accept image or other non-text input, per MiniMax's model card and Fireworks AI's model listing.
MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.1, M2.5, M2.7, and M3); M2 is no longer featured among MiniMax's current models on its site.

bedrock/minimax.minimax-m2.1.description: MiniMax M2.1 is MiniMax's open-weight large language model, an update to M2 with improved reasoning, coding, and instruction following. It targets agentic coding across a wide range of programming languages (including Rust, Java, Go, C++, Kotlin, Objective-C, TypeScript, and JavaScript) plus native Android, iOS, and web app development, and uses an interleaved-thinking reasoning style for long-horizon tool use. It was released December 23, 2025 under a Modified MIT license, with weights published on Hugging Face and GitHub. MiniMax has since released newer M2.5, M2.7, and M3 models in the same line.
disadvantages: Text-only model with no image, audio, or video input.
MiniMax has released newer M2.5, M2.7, and M3 models with further coding and agent improvements since M2.1 launched.

bedrock/minimax.minimax-m2.5.description: MiniMax-M2.5 is MiniMax's mixture-of-experts chat model for agentic and office-productivity work, with 229 billion total parameters and 10 billion active per token, an iterative update to the M2/M2.1 family. It was trained largely through reinforcement learning across more than 200,000 real-world environments and is tuned for coding, tool calling and web search, and document work in Word, Excel and PowerPoint. MiniMax released it on February 12, 2026 under a Modified MIT license; a faster 'M2.5-Lightning' variant trades a higher price for higher throughput.
disadvantages: Text only; no image or audio input.
Artificial Analysis measured a higher hallucination rate (88%) than the prior M2.1 (67%), alongside only a modest accuracy gain (25% vs. 22%).

bedrock/mistral.devstral-2-123b.description: Devstral 2 123B is Mistral AI's 123-billion-parameter dense coding model, released December 9, 2025 as the larger of two Devstral 2 models (alongside a 24B 'Small' version) and the successor generation to the original Devstral. Mistral built it for agentic software-engineering work -- exploring codebases, coordinating multi-file changes, and debugging -- with tool-calling support for coding-agent frameworks such as Cline, Claude Code, OpenHands, and SWE-Agent. It supports a 256,000-token context window and is released under a modified MIT license.
disadvantages: No vision/image input mentioned for this 123B model; Mistral's smaller Devstral Small 2 (24B) supports image input instead.
Modified MIT license bars use by, or on behalf of, a company with more than $20 million in monthly revenue without a separate commercial license from Mistral.

bedrock/mistral.magistral-small-2509.description: Magistral Small 2509 (version 1.2) is Mistral AI's 24-billion-parameter open-weight reasoning model, released September 2025 and built on Mistral Small 3.2, fine-tuned on Magistral Medium's reasoning traces and further refined with reinforcement learning. It adds a vision encoder for multimodal (text and image) input and uses [THINK]/[/THINK] tags to structure chain-of-thought for math, coding and logic tasks, and Mistral documents support across 24 languages. It is licensed under Apache 2.0 for self-deployment. Per Mistral's own model-lifecycle documentation, this version (API id magistral-small-2509) is deprecated, with Mistral Small 4 named as the recommended successor for new integrations.
disadvantages: Deprecated by Mistral AI (deprecation date April 30, 2026), which recommends Mistral Small 4 for new integrations — the catalog's deprecation_date field is currently empty for this model, so this is flagged here rather than in the structured facts.

bedrock/mistral.mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.description: Mixtral 8x7B Instruct is Mistral AI's instruction-tuned version of the Mixtral 8x7B sparse mixture-of-experts model, released December 11, 2023 alongside the base checkpoint under an Apache 2.0 license and fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization (DPO). It has 46.7 billion total parameters with 12.9 billion active per token and a 32K-token context window, and Mistral's launch post reports fluency in English, French, Italian, German and Spanish. Mistral deprecated the Mixtral 8x7B family on its own hosted platform (La Plateforme) on November 30, 2024 and retired it March 30, 2025, recommending Mistral Small 4 as a replacement; the open weights remain Active on Amazon Bedrock and available through Fireworks AI.
disadvantages: Deprecated on Mistral's own hosted API as of November 30, 2024 and retired March 30, 2025, with Mistral recommending Mistral Small 4 as a replacement.
Its Hugging Face model card states 'the model does not have any moderation mechanisms,' with no built-in content filtering.

bedrock/mistral.voxtral-mini-3b-2507.description: Voxtral Mini 3B is Mistral AI's compact speech-to-text and voice-understanding model, released under the Apache 2.0 license on July 15, 2025 as a smaller sibling to Voxtral Small. Built on the Ministral 3B text backbone, it performs automatic speech transcription with language detection, answers questions about audio, summarizes it, and can trigger function calls directly from voice, while retaining Ministral 3B's text understanding. Mistral documents support for audio up to 30 minutes for transcription or 40 minutes for understanding, and names eight core languages: English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Hindi, German, Dutch and Italian. Mistral deprecated this original Voxtral Mini (2507) version on its own platform in February 2026 in favor of Voxtral Mini Transcribe 2, but Amazon Bedrock, which offers it as mistral.voxtral-mini-3b-2507 for chat completions, still lists the model as Active with an end-of-life no sooner than July 2026.
disadvantages: Superseded on Mistral's own platform by Voxtral Mini Transcribe 2 since a February 2026 deprecation, though the Bedrock-hosted version used here remains Active (Mistral AI Voxtral Mini docs; Amazon Bedrock Voxtral Mini 3B 2507 model card).

Amazon Bedrock's model card lists only client-side tool calling as supported for this model on the bedrock-mantle endpoint, not server-side tool calling, and does not list support for the Responses API (Amazon Bedrock Voxtral Mini 3B 2507 model card).

Documented for eight languages with strong performance (English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Hindi, German, Dutch, Italian); Mistral's phrasing ('to name a few') implies broader coverage, but no fuller language list is given (Mistral AI Voxtral blog).

bedrock/moonshot.kimi-k2-thinking.description: Kimi K2 Thinking is Moonshot AI's reasoning-focused chat and agent model, sharing Kimi K2's 1-trillion-parameter, 32-billion-activated mixture-of-experts architecture but adding an interleaved chain-of-thought 'thinking' mode that reasons between tool calls. Moonshot's model card states it maintains coherent, goal-directed behavior across 200-300 consecutive tool invocations, versus 30-50 steps in prior models, and it ships with native INT4 post-training quantization on its MoE layers for roughly a 2x speed-up in low-latency inference. It takes text-only input and is released under a Modified MIT License. Moonshot's own API platform lists this model's hosted endpoints as discontinued since May 25, 2026 in favor of its newer Kimi K3 model.
disadvantages: Text-only: no vision/image input, per the catalog's modality and Moonshot's model card.
Score on Humanity's Last Exam drops to 23.9% without tool access, versus 44.9% with tools, per Moonshot's model card.

Moonshot's own API platform lists the matching hosted endpoints ('kimi-k2-thinking', 'kimi-k2-thinking-turbo') as discontinued since May 25, 2026, directing users to the newer Kimi K3 model, per Moonshot's Model List page.

Per AWS's documentation, it 'minimizes alterations to the image and should not be used to reimagine an image,' keeping the upscaled result close to the original rather than adding new content. It takes an image and a required text prompt, with optional negative prompt, creativity, seed, and output format parameters.

It is built for complex systems engineering, multi-step reasoning, math, advanced coding, and tool-augmented agentic workflows, with a 200K-token context window and up to 128K tokens of output. It is released under the MIT license.
disadvantages: Text-only: no image or audio input or output support.

cartesia/ink-2.description: Ink-2 is Cartesia's streaming speech-to-text model built for real-time voice agents, launched July 9, 2026. Cartesia describes it as its fastest and most accurate streaming STT, with native turn detection so agents know when a caller has finished speaking without a separate voice-activity-detection step. It accurately transcribes structured data such as phone numbers, dates, and emails, and is currently offered for English, French, Hindi, Japanese, and Spanish with automatic language detection.
disadvantages: Only supports realtime/streaming transcription endpoints; Cartesia's own batch transcription endpoint uses the older Ink-Whisper model instead.
Covers five languages (English, French, Hindi, Japanese, Spanish) versus the 99 languages of Cartesia's older Ink-Whisper model.

cartesia/ink-whisper.description: Ink-Whisper is Cartesia's lower-cost speech-to-text model, used for batch transcription of pre-recorded audio and, via Cartesia's manual-finalization realtime endpoint, for streaming transcription without built-in turn detection (the snapshot ink-whisper-2025-06-04 is documented as stable). Cartesia describes it as more accurate and lower-latency than baseline Whisper, with dynamic chunking for variable-length audio, resilience to background noise and telephony artifacts, and accurate transcription of proper nouns and domain-specific terms. Cartesia's current docs describe it as an older model and point users to Ink-2 for improved turn detection in English voice agents, though Ink-Whisper remains documented and available.
disadvantages: Not available on Cartesia's auto-finalization realtime endpoint with native turn detection, which is exclusive to Ink-2 and Ink-preview; Ink-Whisper is used via the batch endpoint or the manual-finalization realtime endpoint instead.

cartesia/sonic-3.6.description: Sonic-3.6 is Cartesia's text-to-speech model, announced August 27, 2026 as the successor to Sonic-3.5 and now the company's recommended model for production voice agents. It natively supports 44 languages across 61 locales with over 500 preset voices, including new Odia and Urdu voices and Hinglish (Hindi-English) code-switching. Cartesia says it follows the input transcript faithfully while varying pacing, intonation, and pause length to match emotional context, and reports reply latency under 90ms. Cartesia states Sonic-3.5 remains supported as an earlier stable version, so Sonic-3.6 is the newer of the two rather than a forced replacement.
disadvantages: Explicit emotion control via the generation_config.emotion parameter is a beta feature documented as supported for English transcripts only; other languages rely on the model's automatic reading of emotional subtext.

deepseek/deepseek-flash.description: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is DeepSeek's multimodal mixture-of-experts chat model, released September 10, 2026 as the smallest model in a new architecture family and reached via the API model id deepseek-flash. It uses a Causal Encoder-Decoder design with 552 billion backbone parameters but activates only 8 billion for input processing and 16 billion for output generation, and it processes images alongside text natively from pretraining. DeepSeek reports that internal and third-party tests place it ahead of the larger DeepSeek-V4-Pro on performance, cost, speed and total runtime despite the much smaller active-parameter count. It succeeds the earlier DeepSeek-V4-Flash (public beta July 2026); the legacy ids deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are retired and now route to this model, billed at Flash pricing.
disadvantages: No audio input or output; modality is limited to text and images.

deepseek/deepseek-r1.description: DeepSeek-R1 is DeepSeek AI's first-generation reasoning model, released January 2025 and documented in an accompanying arXiv paper (2501.12948) as achieving performance comparable to OpenAI's o1 on math, code and reasoning tasks. It is a 671-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 37 billion active parameters, built from a DeepSeek-V3-Base checkpoint and trained with large-scale reinforcement learning to produce extended chain-of-thought reasoning before its final answer, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository. DeepSeek originally served R1 on its own platform under the deepseek-reasoner model name, but DeepSeek's changelog shows that alias was reassigned away from R1 to DeepSeek-V3.1 as early as August 2025, then to several later V3.x releases; DeepSeek's current API pricing page lists only deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro, with deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner no longer listed at all following their announced 2026-07-24 discontinuation. The open-weight model remains downloadable from DeepSeek directly and, per Bud's catalog, is still served through third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI and Hyperbolic.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's current API documentation no longer lists standalone R1 among its active models; the deepseek-reasoner alias that served R1 was reassigned to DeepSeek-V3.1 in August 2025 (a year before any V4 model existed), and the alias itself was discontinued by 2026-07-24 alongside deepseek-chat.
Superseded on DeepSeek's own reasoning line by the May 2025 DeepSeek-R1-0528 update, which DeepSeek reports scores substantially higher on the same benchmarks.
DeepSeek's usage guidance for R1 recommends against system prompts and a temperature of 0.5-0.7.
Text only; no image or audio input or output, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.

deepseek/deepseek-reasoner.description: DeepSeek-reasoner is an advanced reasoning model developed by DeepSeek, designed for complex reasoning, mathematical problem-solving, and code generation using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. Built on the DeepSeek-V3 architecture with 671 billion total parameters and 37 billion activated per token, it features a 128,000-token context window and open-source MIT licensing. The model emphasizes transparency through detailed reasoning steps and achieves performance comparable to OpenAI's o1 model at 96% lower cost.

DeepSeek's own changelog shows the deepseek-chat endpoint was later upgraded through DeepSeek-V3-0324, V3.1, V3.1-Terminus, V3.2 and V4.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's own changelog shows this model was superseded by DeepSeek-V3-0324, V3.1, V3.1-Terminus, V3.2 and V4, and is no longer served under DeepSeek's default deepseek-chat alias.

deepseek/deepseek-v3.2.description: DeepSeek-V3.2 is DeepSeek's mixture-of-experts chat and reasoning model, with 685 billion parameters per its Hugging Face model card, released December 1, 2025 as the official successor to the experimental DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp. It uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention for cheaper long-context inference and, per DeepSeek's launch announcement, is the first DeepSeek model to combine a 'thinking' mode -- extended reasoning before acting -- with tool use, alongside a faster non-thinking mode. DeepSeek briefly served it as the standard deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner model, but DeepSeek's changelog shows those two names were repointed to the newer DeepSeek-V4-Flash in April 2026 and slated for discontinuation by July 2026, and V4-Flash was itself later retired in favor of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Amazon Bedrock still lists deepseek.v3.2 with an 'Active' lifecycle, a 164K-token context window, and an 8K-token output limit.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's changelog shows the deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner names that served V3.2 were repointed to newer V4 models starting April 2026, with the intervening V4-Flash name itself later retired in favor of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
8,000-token maximum output on Amazon Bedrock.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash was DeepSeek's mid-sized mixture-of-experts chat model, publicly released July 31, 2026 (as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) superseding an April 2026 preview, with 284 billion total parameters and 13 billion active per token per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card. It offered a 1,000,000-token context window, three reasoning-effort levels (low, high, max), and native support for OpenAI's Responses API adapted for Codex integration. DeepSeek retired the model on September 10, 2026: requests sent to the model id deepseek-v4-flash are now automatically served by the newer, multimodal DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and billed at Flash pricing, which is why this id now also accepts image input even though the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash release was text-only.
disadvantages: The original DeepSeek-V4-Flash model was retired by DeepSeek on September 10, 2026; this id is now an alias routed to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rather than a distinct, actively maintained model.
The original release was text-only with no image or audio input; any current multimodal behavior on this id comes solely from the underlying routing to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
use_cases: Agentic coding tasks, with native support for OpenAI's Responses API format adapted for Codex integration.
Tool-calling agent workflows described by DeepSeek as 'daily Agent workflows' at the high reasoning-effort level.

DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card shows its multimodal agent scores approaching or exceeding Claude Opus-4.8's on the same benchmarks, e.g. 83.9 vs. 85.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 59.3 vs. 58.0 on DeepSWE, while matching DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on text-only agent tasks.
deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, released August 21, 2026, was DeepSeek's first experimental multimodal model in the V4 family, described on its own Hugging Face model card as built on the DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture (305 billion parameters) with an added vision encoder and aligner so it can process images and text together. DeepSeek's model card states it achieves comparable performance to DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on text-only agent tasks while substantially improving multimodal agent capabilities, and its own benchmark table shows those multimodal agent scores approaching, and on some benchmarks matching or exceeding, Claude Opus-4.8's scores on the same tests. DeepSeek retired the model on September 10, 2026, and requests to the id deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are now routed to the newer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, billed at Flash pricing.
disadvantages: Explicitly labeled experimental by DeepSeek, as an early multimodal expansion of DeepSeek-V4-Flash still undergoing continued training.
DeepSeek retired this model on September 10, 2026, routing deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp requests to the newer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Scores lower than DeepSeek's later DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on comparable agent benchmarks, e.g. 83.9 vs. 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 59.3 vs. 74.2 on DeepSWE.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro.description: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is DeepSeek's flagship mixture-of-experts chat model, with 1.6 trillion total parameters and 49 billion active per token, reaching general availability on August 13, 2026. It supports a 1,000,000-token context window and three switchable reasoning modes (Non-think, Think High, Think Max), and is built for coding, math, and long-horizon agentic workflows. DeepSeek's own V4.1-Flash announcement cites third-party tests showing the newer, smaller DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (released September 10, 2026) ahead of V4-Pro on performance, cost, speed and total runtime, and DeepSeek has begun phasing out V4-Pro, automatically routing its API requests to V4.1-Flash since September 14, 2026.

elevenlabs/eleven_v3.description: Eleven v3 is ElevenLabs' most expressive text-to-speech model, launched in alpha in June 2025 and made generally available in February 2026, built to produce emotionally nuanced, reactive speech rather than flat narration. elevenlabs/scribe_v2_medical.description: Scribe v2 Medical is ElevenLabs' speech recognition model, a fine-tune of Scribe v2 for medical and clinical audio, that became generally available on September 22, 2026. It improves recognition of drug names, anatomy, pathology, and clinical dictation while matching Scribe v2's accuracy on everyday speech, and supports 90+ languages, entity detection (including PHI categories), speaker diarization, and word-level timestamps through the same batch Speech-to-Text API, request parameters, and pricing as Scribe v2. ElevenLabs intends it for producing draft transcripts of clinical audio, such as clinician-patient conversations, dictation, and intake calls, for review and correction by a healthcare professional; it is not intended to interpret clinical information or provide diagnoses, treatment recommendations, or other clinical guidance.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: UAE-Large-V1 ("Universal AnglE Embedding") is a BERT-based English text embedding model from WhereIsAI, released in December 2023 and trained with the angle-optimized (AnglE) loss described in the paper "AnglE-optimized Text Embeddings" (accepted at ACL 2024). fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 is DeepSeek AI's open-weight language model built specifically for automated formal theorem proving in the Lean 4 proof assistant. Fireworks AI, which hosts the exact model id used here, confirms it serves the larger 671-billion-parameter variant (DeepSeek also publishes a smaller 7-billion-parameter version), built on the DeepSeek-V3-Base architecture. It was trained with a recursive proof-search pipeline: DeepSeek-V3 decomposes theorems into subgoals that a 7B prover model solves, the assembled proofs and reasoning chains form cold-start data, and reinforcement learning with binary correctness feedback follows, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository. It is a mathematics/formal-verification specialist rather than a general-purpose chat model.
disadvantages: A specialist model for formal Lean 4 theorem proving, not a general-purpose chat or instruction-following model.

disadvantages: DeepSeek's model card recommends capping output around 32,768 tokens and notes the model can 'bypass thinking pattern' on some queries, which may reduce answer quality.

DeepSeek's own API changelog labels this reasoning generation 'legacy R1' and discontinued the deepseek-reasoner model id in favor of the DeepSeek-V4 series by July 2026, though the open weights stay available on Hugging Face and via third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI.
use_cases: Mathematical problem-solving with step-by-step reasoning

Complex multi-step reasoning and logic tasks
General text generation with an explicit chain-of-thought 'thinking' step

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is a 1.5-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1, fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B on about 800,000 reasoning traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. It is the smallest model in DeepSeek's R1 distillation family, built to bring R1-style step-by-step reasoning to hardware too limited for the full 671B R1 model. DeepSeek's model card recommends running it without a system prompt at a temperature of 0.5-0.7, and notes the model can sometimes skip its own reasoning step. Both the model weights and DeepSeek's code are released under the MIT License.
disadvantages: Scores 16.9% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench, the lowest of the Qwen-based models in DeepSeek's R1-distill family, per DeepSeek's model card.
DeepSeek's model card says the distilled models can skip their own reasoning step on some queries, which may require forcing the response to start with '<think>\n'.
Text-only reasoning model; its model card documents no vision or tool-use support.
use_cases: Lightweight chain-of-thought reasoning on resource-constrained hardware.
Mathematical problem solving.
Coding assistance and code reasoning at small scale.
Research and experimentation with small-scale distilled reasoning models.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B is a 32-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1, fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen2.5-32B on about 800,000 reasoning traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. It is the largest Qwen-based checkpoint in DeepSeek's R1 distillation family, transferring R1's chain-of-thought reasoning into a dense model that is cheaper to serve than the full 671B R1. fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B is a 7-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1, fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen2.5-Math-7B on about 800,000 reasoning traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat is the supervised-fine-tuned chat version of DeepSeek-V2-Lite, a 16-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 2.4 billion parameters activated per token, which DeepSeek released in May 2024. It uses DeepSeek's Multi-head Latent Attention to compress its key-value cache and DeepSeekMoE for sparse, economical computation; DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card says these let it run BF16 inference on a single 40GB GPU. It is the smaller sibling of the 236-billion-parameter DeepSeek-V2-Chat in the same model family. Model use is governed by DeepSeek's Model License, while the DeepSeek-V2 code is released under the MIT License.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's GitHub repository says the open-source Hugging Face Transformers implementation runs slower than DeepSeek's internal codebase, and recommends vLLM for best performance.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V2.5 is a 236-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts chat and coding model, with about 21 billion parameters activated per token, that DeepSeek released on September 5, 2024. DeepSeek's changelog describes it as merging and upgrading the earlier DeepSeek-V2-Chat and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct models into a single model that combines general conversational ability with coding capability, with better alignment to human preferences and improved writing and instruction-following than either predecessor. Model use is governed by DeepSeek's Model License, while the DeepSeek-V2 code is released under the MIT License.
disadvantages: Its SWE-bench Verified score of 16.8 is lower than the 19 scored by its DeepSeek-Coder-V2-0724 predecessor, per DeepSeek's own benchmark table.

Text-only model; its model card documents no vision input support.

Function calling and tool integration.
Long-form writing and instruction-following tasks.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V3 is DeepSeek's 671-billion-parameter (37 billion activated per token) Mixture-of-Experts chat model, released December 26, 2024 per DeepSeek's own API changelog. DeepSeek's own changelog shows the deepseek-chat endpoint was later upgraded through DeepSeek-V3-0324, V3.1, V3.1-Terminus, V3.2 and V4.

Text only; no image or audio input or output.

Mathematical problem solving.
Document analysis within a 128,000-token context window.

Its Hugging Face model card lists MIT-licensed weights. DeepSeek's own changelog shows the deepseek-chat endpoint has since moved on through DeepSeek-V3.1, V3.1-Terminus and V3.2 to newer DeepSeek-V4 models.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's own changelog shows the deepseek-chat endpoint has since moved on to newer DeepSeek-V4 models, so this checkpoint is no longer served under that default alias.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus is DeepSeek's September 22, 2025 update to DeepSeek-V3.1, per DeepSeek's own API changelog, targeting user-reported issues: mixed Chinese-English text and stray characters, plus further tuning of its Code Agent and Search Agent tool use. fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V3.2 is DeepSeek's mixture-of-experts chat and reasoning model, released December 1, 2025 per DeepSeek's own API changelog as the successor to the experimental DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp (itself DeepSeek's successor to V3.1-Terminus). DeepSeek's own changelog shows the deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner endpoint names have since moved on to newer DeepSeek-V4 models.

Agentic workflows that interleave long-chain reasoning with tool calls.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash was DeepSeek's mid-sized mixture-of-experts chat model, publicly released July 31, 2026 (as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) superseding an April 2026 preview, with 284 billion total parameters and 13 billion active per token per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card. DeepSeek retired the model on September 10, 2026: requests sent to the model id deepseek-v4-flash are now automatically served by the newer, multimodal DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and billed at Flash pricing, which is why this id now also accepts image input even though the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash release was text-only.
disadvantages: The original DeepSeek-V4-Flash model was retired by DeepSeek on September 10, 2026; this id is now an alias routed to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rather than a distinct, actively maintained model.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is the July 31, 2026 production release of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek's mid-sized mixture-of-experts chat model, superseding an earlier April 2026 preview with 'substantially enhanced agentic capabilities' and 304 billion total parameters, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card, which does not give a separate active-parameter figure for this release. It uses a hybrid Compressed Sparse Attention and Heavily Compressed Attention design for a 1,000,000-token context window, three reasoning-effort levels (low, high, max), and a DSpark speculative-decoding module, with native support for OpenAI's Responses API adapted for Codex integration. DeepSeek retired the model on September 10, 2026, routing requests to the model id deepseek-flash (or the legacy deepseek-v4-flash id) to the newer, multimodal DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash instead.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, released August 21, 2026, was DeepSeek's first experimental multimodal model in the V4 family, described on its own Hugging Face model card as built on the DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture (305 billion parameters) with an added vision encoder and aligner so it can process images and text together. DeepSeek's model card states it achieves comparable performance to DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on text-only agent tasks while substantially improving multimodal agent capabilities, and its own benchmark table shows those multimodal agent scores approaching, and on some benchmarks matching or exceeding, Claude Opus-4.8's scores on the same tests. DeepSeek retired the model on September 10, 2026, and requests to the id deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are now routed to the newer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, billed at Flash pricing.
disadvantages: Explicitly labeled experimental by DeepSeek, as an early multimodal expansion of DeepSeek-V4-Flash still undergoing continued training.
DeepSeek retired this model on September 10, 2026, routing deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp requests to the newer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Scores lower than DeepSeek's later DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on comparable agent benchmarks, e.g. 83.9 vs. 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 59.3 vs. 74.2 on DeepSWE.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 is DeepSeek's flagship mixture-of-experts chat model, released August 13, 2026 as the official general-availability version of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, superseding an earlier preview with what DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card describes as 'greatly enhanced agentic capabilities and performance improvements' especially in production use. It has 1.7 trillion parameters, a roughly 1,000,000-token context window, three reasoning-effort levels (low, high, max), and a DSpark speculative-decoding module, with native OpenAI Responses API support optimized for Codex integration. DeepSeek's own DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash launch announcement states that, starting September 14, 2026, all deepseek-v4-pro API requests are automatically routed to the newer, smaller DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at V4.1-Flash's rates, effectively retiring this release for new traffic.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Devstral Small 2505 is a 24-billion-parameter open-weight coding model that Mistral AI released May 21, 2025 in collaboration with All Hands AI, fine-tuned from Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Base-2503. It is built for agentic software-engineering work -- exploring codebases and editing multiple files -- through coding-agent scaffolds such as OpenHands and SWE-Agent, and is light enough to run locally on a single RTX 4090 GPU or a Mac with 32GB RAM. Mistral's own current documentation lists this version (internally 'Devstral Small 1.0', API id devstral-small-2505) as deprecated, with a retirement date of November 30, 2025, in favor of later Devstral and Mistral Small/Medium releases.
disadvantages: Mistral's models-overview documentation currently lists this version (devstral-small-2505) as deprecated, with a retirement date of November 30, 2025.
Text-only input and output; the vision encoder was removed from its Mistral-Small-3.1-24B base.
Superseded on Mistral's own roadmap by Devstral Small 1.1 (2507) and Devstral 2, per Mistral's documentation.
use_cases: Agentic software-engineering tasks: codebase exploration, multi-file edits, and bug fixing via coding-agent scaffolds.
Local or on-device deployment for privacy-sensitive repositories.
Integration into IDEs and coding copilots via tool/function calling.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Dobby-Mini-Unhinged-Plus-Llama-3.1-8B is an 8-billion-parameter chat model from Sentient (SentientAGI), fine-tuned from Meta's Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to have a deliberately casual, opinionated, pro-crypto 'unhinged' personality rather than a neutral corporate-assistant tone. It is Sentient's improved successor to Dobby-Mini-Unhinged-Llama-3.1-8B, with changes the maker describes as targeting general utility -- formatting, multi-turn performance, and tone -- while keeping baseline Llama 3.1 academic performance. It remains governed by Meta's Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement.
disadvantages: Knowledge cutoff of December 2023, inherited from the Llama 3.1 base model.
Deliberately casual tone that can include profanity and strong opinions rather than neutral assistant behavior; Sentient says investment or legal opinions from it require independent verification.
Governed by Meta's Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement rather than a fully permissive open-source license.
use_cases: General conversational chat emphasizing personality and authenticity over a formal, neutral assistant tone.
Multi-turn dialogue with a distinctive, opinionated character.

advantages: Maintains comparable scores to base Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on standard benchmarks including MMLU-Pro, GPQA, and BBH, per Sentient's model card.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Dobby-Unhinged-Llama-3.3-70B is a 70-billion-parameter chat model from Sentient (SentientAGI), fine-tuned from Meta's Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct to have a deliberately blunt, opinionated, pro-crypto 'unhinged' personality instead of a neutral corporate-assistant tone. Sentient positions it for companion and social agents rather than as a general safety-first assistant, and states it keeps comparable scores to the base Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct model on standard benchmarks such as MMLU-Pro, GPQA, and BBH. It remains governed by Meta's Llama 3.3 Community License Agreement.
disadvantages: Reduced neutrality by design: Sentient says the model keeps its stated opinions rather than adopting neutral or anti-crypto framing when prompted.
Knowledge cutoff of December 2023, inherited from the Llama 3.3 base model.
Deliberately unfiltered tone, including profanity and strong opinions; Sentient says users are responsible for assessing output accuracy.
use_cases: Companion and social agents designed to sound more human and opinionated than a standard assistant.
Entertainment chatbots and social-media personas.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Dolphin 2.9.2 Qwen2 72B is a 72-billion-parameter chat model from Cognitive Computations (Eric Hartford, Lucas Atkins, and Fernando Fernandes), fine-tuned from Alibaba's Qwen2-72B on 14 instruction, coding, math, and agentic tool-use datasets in ChatML format, using selective full-weight fine-tuning of layers identified by the project's 'Laser Scanner' technique. Like other Dolphin releases, the makers filtered alignment and safety training out of the data, producing a highly compliant 'uncensored' model that they say requires an added alignment layer before being deployed as a service. It is licensed under Qwen2's Tongyi Qianwen license.
disadvantages: Deliberately uncensored: the makers filtered alignment and bias out of the training data, state it 'will be highly compliant to any requests, even unethical ones,' and recommend adding an alignment layer before deployment.
Fine-tuned at an 8,192-token sequence length, well below the 128k context the Qwen2-72B base model supports.
Licensed under Qwen2's Tongyi Qianwen license rather than a standard permissive open-source license.

Math word-problem solving.
Early-stage agentic tool use and function calling.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Ember-1 is a reasoning-focused language model from Fireworks AI's research team, built on Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 foundation using a mixture-of-experts architecture. It is trained to reproduce Kimi K3's response quality while spending far fewer tokens on internal reasoning, and it accepts both text and image input alongside function calling. Fireworks positions it for agentic coding and other multi-turn, reasoning-heavy production workloads where long chain-of-thought traces inflate token usage and cost. As of September 2026 it is offered as a Research Preview on Fireworks Serverless, with enterprise fine-tuning support still being rolled out.
disadvantages: Offered only as a Research Preview as of September 2026, so behavior, pricing, and availability may still change.
Fireworks' model listing states fine-tuning, embeddings, and reranker functionality are not supported for this model.

Production workloads needing long-context reasoning together with image input

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT is an instruction-tuned language model from Baidu's ERNIE 4.5 family, released as open weights in Transformer-style PyTorch format (the '-PT' suffix distinguishes it from Baidu's PaddlePaddle-format release of the same checkpoint). It uses a heterogeneous mixture-of-experts architecture with 21B total parameters and 3B activated per token, drawn from 64 text experts (6 active per token) plus 64 vision experts and 2 shared experts across 28 layers, and is trained for text generation in English and Chinese. Baidu reports it achieves competitive performance against Qwen3-30B-A3B despite having roughly 30% fewer total parameters.
disadvantages: Baidu's own model card does not publish quantitative benchmark score tables for this specific variant.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: FireFunction V1 is an open-weight function-calling model from Fireworks AI, built on Mixtral-8x7B and released in February 2024 under the Apache 2.0 license. It is designed for structured output generation and routing decisions across up to 20 function specifications in a single turn, and supports a tool_choice value of "any" that forces a function call, a mode Fireworks says GPT-4 lacked at the model's release. It is not optimized for general multi-turn conversation or for parallel or nested function calls within one response. As of September 2026 it remains listed as available ("Ready") on Fireworks' own model page, though Fireworks has since released a newer firefunction-v2 model in the same family.
disadvantages: Not optimized for general multi-turn conversation or for parallel or nested function calls within a single response; Fireworks recommends breaking such cases into sequential messages.
Released in February 2024 as a free beta; Fireworks has since released a newer firefunction-v2 model in the same family.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: FireFunction-v2 is an open-weights function-calling model built by Fireworks AI on top of Meta's Llama 3 70B Instruct, released June 17, 2024. It is tuned for real-world agentic use -- multi-turn conversation, instruction following, and parallel function calling -- rather than narrowly overfitting to function-calling benchmarks, so it also keeps much of Llama 3's general chat ability. Fireworks reports it is competitive with GPT-4o on a combined function-calling benchmark medley (0.81 vs 0.80) and reliably handles up to 30 function specifications in a single call.
disadvantages: Not optimized for more than 100 function specifications or for nested function calling, per its Hugging Face model card.
MT-Bench score of 0.84 trails GPT-4o's 0.93 and its own Llama 3 70B Instruct base's 0.89, indicating a general-chat quality gap versus those models.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: FireLLaVA-13B is a vision-language model released by Fireworks AI on January 18, 2024, combining the LLaVA architecture's Vicuna v1.5 13B language model with an OpenAI CLIP-ViT vision encoder. fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: gpt-oss-20b is OpenAI's smaller open-weight reasoning model, released under an Apache 2.0 license in August 2025 alongside the larger gpt-oss-120b. It uses a mixture-of-experts transformer architecture with 21 billion total parameters and 3.6 billion active parameters per token, and is designed to run within 16GB of memory using native MXFP4 quantization of its MoE weights, suiting local or specialized deployment. The model supports low, medium and high reasoning-effort settings, exposes its full chain of thought, and is trained for agentic tool use including function calling, Python code execution and web browsing. It requires OpenAI's harmony response format to operate correctly.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: gpt-oss-safeguard-120b is OpenAI's open-weight reasoning model for safety classification, released as a research preview in October 2025 under an Apache 2.0 license. It is a reasoning fine-tune of gpt-oss-120b (117 billion total / 5.1 billion active parameters) that takes a user-supplied written policy and a piece of content, classifies the content against that policy, and returns its chain-of-thought reasoning alongside the decision rather than only a score. It supports low, medium and high reasoning-effort settings and, like the base gpt-oss models, requires OpenAI's harmony response format. OpenAI recommends the base gpt-oss models for non-safety use cases.
disadvantages: Released as a research preview, per OpenAI's launch post.
Performance was mixed on the ToxicChat benchmark, where gpt-5-thinking marginally outperformed gpt-oss-safeguard-120b, per OpenAI's launch post.

OpenAI notes traditional classifiers trained on large labeled datasets can still outperform gpt-oss-safeguard, and its reasoning process is more computationally expensive to run at scale, per OpenAI's launch post.
Requires OpenAI's harmony response format; OpenAI recommends the base gpt-oss models for applications outside safety classification, per OpenAI's Hugging Face model card.

Auditable, policy-based content classification where explainability matters more than speed

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Hermes 2 Pro on Mistral 7B is Nous Research's 7-billion-parameter chat model, an upgraded retrain of Nous Hermes 2 built on Mistral-7B-v0.1 and trained on a cleaned version of the OpenHermes 2.5 dataset plus new in-house function-calling and JSON-mode datasets, developed in partnership with Fireworks.AI. It uses the ChatML prompt format with a dedicated system-prompt structure for multi-turn function calling and structured JSON output. Nous Research has since released newer Hermes generations (Hermes 4 and Hermes 4.3) on Hugging Face.
disadvantages: Built on the original Mistral-7B-v0.1 base model; Nous Research has since released newer Hermes generations (Hermes 4, Hermes 4.3) on Hugging Face.
The model card's own tables show lower scores on more complex reasoning suites: AGIEval averages 44.52 and BigBench averages 41.65.
The model card states elsewhere that function-calling accuracy is 90%, a point lower than the 91% given in its dedicated evaluation section.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Inkling is a general-purpose multimodal chat model from Thinking Machines Lab, released in July 2026. It is a 66-layer decoder-only transformer with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts feed-forward backbone (975B total parameters, 41B active per token, routing each token to 6 of 256 experts plus 2 shared experts), natively accepting text, image, and audio input and generating text output. The model card states it is intended for use in English and other languages, and across multiple coding languages, for developers building conversational, agentic/tool-use, coding-assistant, and retrieval-augmented-generation applications. It is released with open weights under an Apache 2.0 license.
disadvantages: The model card states it "may exhibit general limitations common to foundation models, including hallucination... occasional failures to follow instructions precisely, and degraded performance in long multi-turn conversations."
Knowledge is limited to information available as of its training cutoff, per the model card.
The maker advises against deploying it in medical, legal, or safety-critical decision-making without additional fine-tuning, domain-specific validation, and human oversight, per the model card.

advantages: Scores 70.1 on MMMU and 75.1 on MathVista, per OpenGVLab's InternVL3 launch blog benchmark tables.
Scores 95.4 on DocVQA (test) and 89.2 on ChartQA (test avg.) for OCR, chart, and document understanding, per the same blog.
Combines an InternViT-6B-448px-V2_5 vision encoder with a Qwen2.5-32B language model, and adds Variable Visual Position Encoding for long-context multimodal input, per the model card.
fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: InternVL3-38B is a vision-language chat model from OpenGVLab (Shanghai AI Laboratory), released April 11, 2025 as part of the InternVL3 series. It follows a ViT-MLP-LLM design, combining an InternViT-6B-448px-V2_5 vision encoder with a Qwen2.5-32B language model (38B parameters total), trained with Native Multimodal Pre-Training and Mixed Preference Optimization. It handles multimodal reasoning, OCR/chart/document understanding, multi-image and video input, visual grounding, and GUI-agent tasks. OpenGVLab has since released the newer InternVL3.5 series (August 2025).
disadvantages: OpenGVLab has since released InternVL3.5 (announced August 2025), a newer generation in the same InternVL series, per the OpenGVLab/InternVL GitHub README.

OCR, chart, and document understanding
Multi-image and video comprehension
Visual grounding and GUI agent tasks
Multilingual multimodal understanding

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: InternVL3-78B is a vision-language chat model from OpenGVLab (Shanghai AI Laboratory), released April 11, 2025 as the largest model in the InternVL3 series. OpenGVLab has since released the newer InternVL3.5 series (August 2025).

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: InternVL3-8B is a multimodal vision-language model from OpenGVLab (Shanghai AI Laboratory) that pairs an InternViT-300M-448px-V2.5 vision encoder with a Qwen2.5-7B language model in a ViT-MLP-LLM design, natively built for image, video and text understanding. OpenGVLab's InternVL project repository lists InternVL3.5 (released August 2025) as the current generation superseding the InternVL3 series.
disadvantages: This catalog entry exposes only text input and output, even though InternVL3-8B is natively a vision-language model.
Superseded within OpenGVLab's own family by the newer InternVL3.5 series (August 2025), which the maker says improves versatility, reasoning and inference efficiency.

Conversational, instruction-following chat assistance

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Japanese Stable Diffusion XL is a text-to-image diffusion model from Stability AI, fine-tuned from SDXL 1.0 using Orthogonal Fine-tuning (OFT) so it can take prompts written in Japanese and generate images reflecting Japanese language and cultural expression. Stability AI's model card notes it shares SDXL's known limitation of not being able to render legible text in images. It is released under the Stability AI Community License, with commercial use requiring a separate agreement.
disadvantages: Cannot render legible text in generated images, per Stability AI's model card.
Commercial use requires a separate license agreement under the Stability AI Community License.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: KAT-Coder is Kwaipilot's (Kuaishou's AI team) flagship agentic coding model, built for real-world software-engineering work such as feature implementation, bug fixing, refactoring and test generation. Fireworks AI, which hosts the version served under this id as "KAT-Coder-Pro V1", lists it at 235 billion parameters with a 262,000-token context window. Unlike Kwaipilot's open-weight KAT-Dev models, KAT-Coder itself is not open-weight; Kwaipilot's own site says it is reached via an API key on the StreamLake platform.
disadvantages: Not open-weight; Kwaipilot's site says KAT-Coder is reached only via an API key on the StreamLake platform, unlike its open-weight KAT-Dev siblings.
use_cases: Feature implementation and enhancement in existing codebases
Bug fixing and code refactoring
Automated test generation and code understanding
Agentic software-engineering workflows with sandboxed tool use

Released under the Apache 2.0 license, permitting broad reuse.
fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: KAT-Dev (published on Hugging Face as Kwaipilot/KAT-Dev) is a 33-billion-parameter open-weight coding model from Kwaipilot, Kuaishou's AI team, built on Qwen3-32B through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning stages for software-engineering tasks. Kwaipilot released it as the open-source counterpart to its proprietary KAT-Coder model, incorporating teacher trajectories annotated by human engineers during training. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license.
disadvantages: Kwaipilot notes that extensive mid-training for tool use showed limited direct performance gains on current leaderboards for this model.

disadvantages: Explicitly labeled experimental by Kwaipilot, released to demonstrate research techniques rather than as a finished product.
use_cases: Software-engineering and code-generation tasks evaluated as an autonomous SWE-agent
Research into large-scale reinforcement-learning training techniques for coding models

Moonshot's Hugging Face card lists Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905 as this checkpoint's designated 'new_version', pointing users to a newer release.

Terminal-based coding agents.
General tool-calling chat workflows.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2 Thinking is Moonshot AI's reasoning-focused chat and agent model, sharing Kimi K2's 1-trillion-parameter, 32-billion-activated mixture-of-experts architecture but adding an interleaved chain-of-thought 'thinking' mode that reasons between tool calls. Moonshot's model card states it maintains coherent, goal-directed behavior across 200-300 consecutive tool invocations, versus 30-50 steps in prior models, and it ships with native INT4 post-training quantization on its MoE layers for roughly a 2x speed-up in low-latency inference. It takes text-only input and is released under a Modified MIT License. Moonshot's own API platform lists this model's hosted endpoints as discontinued since May 25, 2026 in favor of its newer Kimi K3 model.
disadvantages: Text-only: no vision/image input, per the catalog's modality and Moonshot's model card.

Moonshot's own card notes the hosted chat mode on kimi.com uses a reduced tool subset and fewer steps than the benchmarked configuration.

Moonshot's own API platform lists the matching hosted endpoints ('kimi-k2-thinking', 'kimi-k2-thinking-turbo') as discontinued since May 25, 2026, directing users to the newer Kimi K3 model, per Moonshot's Model List page.
use_cases: Deep-research agents that browse the web and call tools across long multi-step tasks.
Autonomous coding agents needing sustained multi-step tool use.
Competition math and STEM problem solving.
Long-horizon agentic workflows requiring hundreds of coherent tool calls.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2.5 is Moonshot AI's agentic chat model, built via continual pretraining of Kimi K2 on roughly 15 trillion additional image-and-text tokens, on the same 1-trillion-parameter, 32-billion-activated mixture-of-experts architecture. Moonshot's Hugging Face card, dated January 29, 2026, describes it as natively multimodal -- unifying vision and text, thinking and non-thinking modes, and single- and multi-agent execution -- and adds an 'Agent Swarm' feature that decomposes a task into parallel sub-tasks run by dynamically instantiated sub-agents. It is released under a Modified MIT License. Moonshot's own later Kimi K2.6 model card reports higher scores than K2.5 on several agentic benchmarks.
disadvantages: Superseded within Moonshot's own lineup by the later Kimi K2.6 release, whose model card reports higher scores than K2.5 on SWE-Bench Pro (58.6 vs 50.7) and Humanity's Last Exam with tools (54.0 vs 50.2).
Moonshot's own API platform lists 'kimi-k2.5' as discontinued since August 31, 2026, directing users to the newer Kimi K3 model, per Moonshot's Model List page.
use_cases: Vision-based code generation from UI designs and visual specifications.
Multi-step tool calling and interleaved reasoning for autonomous agent tasks.
Cross-modal reasoning over combined image-and-text input.
Large multi-agent workflows via Agent Swarm orchestration.

advantages: Scores 54.0% on Humanity's Last Exam (Full, with tools), up from 50.2% for Kimi K2.5, per Moonshot's model card.
Scores 58.6% on SWE-Bench Pro, up from 50.7% for Kimi K2.5, per Moonshot's model card.
Scores 92.5 F1 on DeepSearchQA, up from 89.0 for Kimi K2.5, per Moonshot's model card.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2.6 is Moonshot AI's native multimodal agentic chat model, an update to Kimi K2.5 on the same 1-trillion-parameter, 32-billion-activated mixture-of-experts architecture with a MoonViT vision encoder, adding stronger long-horizon coding, coding-driven design, and 'swarm-based' multi-agent task orchestration. Moonshot's model card enables thinking mode by default (with an optional instant mode) and reports improvements over Kimi K2.5 on several agentic benchmarks. It takes text and image input -- video chat is described as experimental and limited to Moonshot's official API -- and is released under a Modified MIT License.
disadvantages: Video chat support is described by Moonshot as experimental and limited to the official API, not a core capability.
Moonshot's newer Kimi K2.7-Code, built upon K2.6, reduces thinking-token usage by roughly 30% compared with K2.6 on coding tasks, per Kimi K2.7-Code's model card.
use_cases: Long-horizon autonomous coding across large codebases.
Coding-driven UI and visual design from screenshots or mockups.
Swarm-based multi-agent task orchestration.
Multi-turn agent workflows that need reasoning preserved across turns.

advantages: Reduces thinking-token usage by about 30% compared to its Kimi K2.6 predecessor while improving real-world long-horizon coding performance, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 81.1 on MCPMark-Verified and 76.0 on MCP Atlas, indicating strong tool-use via MCPs (Model Context Protocol), per its Hugging Face model card.
Supports native INT4 quantization and is documented for deployment with vLLM, SGLang, and KTransformers, per its Hugging Face model card.
Integrates with the Kimi Code CLI as its recommended agent framework for coding workflows, per its Hugging Face model card.
fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2.7 Code is a coding-focused, agentic large language model from Moonshot AI, built on the Kimi K2.6 checkpoint within Moonshot's Kimi K2 series. disadvantages: Like other VLM-based OCR models, it can hallucinate or drop content, per the model card's Limitations section.

With PairRM-best-of-16 post-processing (generating 16 responses and selecting the highest-scoring one), Snorkel AI reports a score of 34.86 on AlpacaEval 2.0, ranked 2nd at the time of publication.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Snorkel-Mistral-PairRM-DPO is Snorkel AI's demonstration model showing how a base LLM can be programmatically aligned using a smaller reward model instead of hand-labeled preference data. Starting from Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, Snorkel AI generated five response variations per prompt from UltraFeedback, reranked them with the PairRM reward model, and updated the LLM with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on the best- and worst-ranked responses, repeating this cycle three times. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license and is presented as a demonstration of this alignment approach rather than a production-ready, moderated model.
disadvantages: The model card states it does not have any moderation mechanisms and lacks guardrails for deployment in environments requiring moderated outputs.
Snorkel AI describes this release as a demonstration of programmatic alignment rather than a production model, per the model card.
The model card notes the AlpacaEval 2.0 judge (gpt-4-turbo) is biased toward longer responses, which the authors say may be a factor in the model's higher ranking.
use_cases: General-purpose instruction-following and conversational chat
Demonstrating reward-model-based (PairRM) alignment as an alternative to human-labeled preference data
Base model for further fine-tuning or alignment experiments

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: SDXL 1.0 (Stable Diffusion XL 1.0) is Stability AI's text-to-image diffusion model, released July 26, 2023 and described by Stability AI as its flagship open image-generation model at the time. It is distributed under the CreativeML Open RAIL++-M license.
disadvantages: The Hugging Face model card states it cannot render legible text and struggles with compositional tasks such as spatial relationships.

Stability AI positions it as a foundational base model for further fine-tuning rather than an instruction-following assistant.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2.5 is Moonshot AI's agentic chat model, built via continual pretraining of Kimi K2 on roughly 15 trillion additional image-and-text tokens, on the same 1-trillion-parameter, 32-billion-activated mixture-of-experts architecture. Moonshot's Hugging Face card, dated January 29, 2026, describes it as natively multimodal -- unifying vision and text, thinking and non-thinking modes, and single- and multi-agent execution -- and adds an 'Agent Swarm' feature that decomposes a task into parallel sub-tasks run by dynamically instantiated sub-agents. It is released under a Modified MIT License. Moonshot's own later Kimi K2.6 model card reports higher scores than K2.5 on several agentic benchmarks.
disadvantages: Superseded within Moonshot's own lineup by the later Kimi K2.6 release, whose model card reports higher scores than K2.5 on SWE-Bench Pro (58.6 vs 50.7) and Humanity's Last Exam with tools (54.0 vs 50.2).
Moonshot's own API platform lists 'kimi-k2.5' as discontinued since August 31, 2026, directing users to the newer Kimi K3 model, per Moonshot's Model List page.
use_cases: Vision-based code generation from UI designs and visual specifications.
Multi-step tool calling and interleaved reasoning for autonomous agent tasks.
Cross-modal reasoning over combined image-and-text input.
Large multi-agent workflows via Agent Swarm orchestration.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2.6 is Moonshot AI's native multimodal agentic chat model, an update to Kimi K2.5 on the same 1-trillion-parameter, 32-billion-activated mixture-of-experts architecture with a MoonViT vision encoder, adding stronger long-horizon coding, coding-driven design, and 'swarm-based' multi-agent task orchestration. Moonshot's model card enables thinking mode by default (with an optional instant mode) and reports improvements over Kimi K2.5 on several agentic benchmarks. It takes text and image input -- video chat is described as experimental and limited to Moonshot's official API -- and is released under a Modified MIT License.
disadvantages: Video chat support is described by Moonshot as experimental and limited to the official API, not a core capability.
Moonshot's newer Kimi K2.7-Code, built upon K2.6, reduces thinking-token usage by roughly 30% compared with K2.6 on coding tasks, per Kimi K2.7-Code's model card.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Kimi K2.7 Code is a coding-focused, agentic large language model from Moonshot AI, built on the Kimi K2.6 checkpoint within Moonshot's Kimi K2 series. Fireworks AI, which hosts the model, states its serverless offering begins deprecating the model on September 25, 2026, recommending Kimi K3 or GLM-5.3 as replacements for serverless workloads.
disadvantages: Fireworks AI states its serverless offering begins deprecating this model on September 25, 2026, recommending Kimi K3 or GLM-5.3 as replacements; on-demand GPU deployments remain available.
Scores 62.0 on Kimi Code Bench v2, versus a 69.0 score it reports for GPT-5.5 on the same benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: MiniMax-M2.1 is MiniMax's text-only Mixture-of-Experts follow-up to MiniMax-M2, again built with roughly 230 billion total parameters and about 10 billion activated per token. MiniMax describes it as more than a parameter update, aimed at stronger real-world performance on systems, backend, web, mobile, and office-style coding tasks plus multilingual, agent-driven workflows, with faster and more concise responses than M2. It supports function calling and agent scaffolding for tool-using workflows. MiniMax has since released newer text models (M2.5, M2.7, and M3), and M2.1 no longer appears among MiniMax's current models on its site.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: MiniMax-M3 is MiniMax's natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts flagship model, released in June 2026, with roughly 428 billion total parameters and about 23 billion activated per token across 128 routed experts. MiniMax trained it on text and images together from the start rather than adding vision later, and built it around a new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) mechanism for long-context efficiency, natively supporting up to about 1,048,576 tokens. It offers a toggleable reasoning ('thinking') mode and is aimed at coding, long-horizon agentic tool use, and multimodal understanding, and is currently MiniMax's newest and most prominently featured text/multimodal model.
disadvantages: Bud's hosted providers serve roughly 512K tokens of context for this model, well below the ~1,048,576-token native context MiniMax describes, per MiniMax's GitHub card and Together AI's listing.
Released only a few months before this write-up (June 2026), so independent, longer-term evaluation is limited.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Muse Glimmer is a 30-billion-parameter dense model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, released August 10, 2026 with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license. It pairs a causal transformer language model with a dedicated vision-transformer perception encoder for image and document understanding, and is tuned for tool calling, coding, and long-running, multi-step agentic workflows intended to run locally on a single consumer GPU. Meta trained it on data from more than 100 languages and reports it comparing favorably to Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on agentic, coding, multimodal, safety and reasoning benchmarks.
disadvantages: Meta's own safety testing found a 28.4% attack success rate on the Siren AgentDojo prompt-injection benchmark, alongside 94.2% task utility.
Meta states performance may degrade on less-represented languages despite training on data from more than 100 languages.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Nemotron 3 Ultra is the largest model in NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 family, released June 4, 2026 as a mixture-of-experts model with 550 billion total parameters and 55 billion active parameters per token, built on a hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture with NVIDIA's LatentMoE design and multi-token-prediction layers for native speculative decoding. NVIDIA states it supports up to 1 million tokens of context and targets agentic and reasoning workloads. This catalog entry serves an NVFP4-quantized checkpoint, which NVIDIA describes as 'post-trained and NVFP4 quantized,' alongside its full-precision BF16 release.
disadvantages: A very large model at 550 billion total / 55 billion active parameters, requiring substantial multi-GPU infrastructure to serve even in NVFP4-quantized form.
NVIDIA's public research pages give only relative throughput comparisons, not specific accuracy benchmark percentages, for this model.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Nemotron Lightning 3.5 30B A3B is a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model from NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 family, with about 3 billion parameters active per token. It uses a hybrid architecture interleaving Mamba-2, mixture-of-experts and attention layers for efficient long-context inference, and includes multi-token-prediction (MTP) among its speculative-decoding options for low-latency serving. NVIDIA's model card states the model produces an explicit reasoning trace before its final response, with reasoning behavior configurable through the chat template, and that it supports function calling but not image input.
disadvantages: Does not support image input or embeddings via its Fireworks hosted listing.

NVIDIA describes this BF16 release as reference weights intended primarily for customization, post-training and research rather than direct production inference, recommending its NVFP4-quantized release for production use instead.

fireworks_ai-embedding-models/fireworks_.description: Nomic Embed Text v1 is an open-weight text embedding model from Nomic AI, built on a long-context BERT-style encoder with an 8192-token input length. It converts text into dense vectors for semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, clustering, and classification, using task-specific prefixes such as `search_document` and `search_query`. Nomic reports it surpasses OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 and text-embedding-3-small on the MTEB benchmark, and releases the model weights, training code, and training data openly under Apache 2.0.
disadvantages: Requires a task-specific prefix (e.g. `search_document`, `search_query`) before embedding, rather than working prefix-free (Nomic AI).
Documented as an English-language model (Nomic AI).

Nomic releases the weights, training code, and training data openly under Apache 2.0.
