advantages: Speechmatics documents Enhanced as delivering the highest accuracy of its two real-time operating points, recommending it for single-language work such as medical, legal or subtitling transcription.
Supports 55+ languages and language packs, each covering multiple accents and dialects, plus bilingual packs and translation to/from English for most languages.
Real-time speaker diarization labels up to 50 speakers by default, configurable up to 100.
Also supports custom dictionaries, turn detection for voice assistants, and speaker identification through voice-profile enrollment on streaming audio.
speechmatics/real-time-enhanced.description: Speechmatics' Enhanced operating point for real-time (streaming) speech-to-text, delivered over a WebSocket connection. It is the higher-accuracy of Speechmatics' two real-time models: the maker recommends it for single-language audio such as medical, legal or subtitling work where accuracy matters more than raw throughput. Enhanced supports 55+ languages and language packs (each covering multiple accents and dialects), plus bilingual packs and translation to/from English for most languages. It is feature-identical to Speechmatics' Standard operating point and differs only in its accuracy/speed trade-off.
disadvantages: Automatic language detection is available only with Speechmatics' Batch transcription, not Realtime, so the language or language pack must be set explicitly for streaming audio.
Standard, Speechmatics' other real-time operating point, is documented as faster and prioritizing throughput; Enhanced trades some speed for its higher accuracy.
use_cases: Medical transcription
Legal transcription
Live subtitling and captioning
Voice assistants that use turn detection to know when a speaker has finished talking

advantages: Speechmatics documents Standard as its fastest real-time operating point, prioritizing throughput over the maximum accuracy that its Enhanced operating point targets.
Feature-identical to Enhanced: supports the same 55+ languages and language packs, bilingual packs, and translation to/from English for most languages.
Real-time speaker diarization labels up to 50 speakers by default, configurable up to 100.
Also supports custom dictionaries, turn detection for voice assistants, and speaker identification through voice-profile enrollment on streaming audio.
speechmatics/real-time-standard.description: Speechmatics' Standard operating point for real-time (streaming) speech-to-text, delivered over a WebSocket connection. It is the faster, higher-throughput of Speechmatics' two real-time models; the maker recommends it when throughput or latency matter more than maximum accuracy, such as archival transcription, content indexing or large-scale captioning. Standard is feature-identical to Speechmatics' Enhanced operating point, supporting the same 55+ languages and language packs, bilingual packs, translation to/from English, and real-time speaker diarization, differing from Enhanced only in its accuracy/speed trade-off.
disadvantages: Speechmatics documents Standard as trading maximum accuracy for throughput; its Enhanced operating point is recommended instead when accuracy matters most, such as medical or legal work.
Automatic language detection is available only with Speechmatics' Batch transcription, not Realtime, so the language or language pack must be set explicitly for streaming audio.
use_cases: Archival transcription
Content indexing
Large-scale live captioning

advantages: Speechmatics states the first audio chunk typically returns in under 200ms, with subsequent chunks generated faster than real time.
Supports streaming output so audio can start playing before the full response has finished generating.
Speechmatics' enterprise plan lists custom voice development and custom language development as available options.
speechmatics/text-to-speech.description: Speechmatics' Text-to-Speech API converts text into spoken audio for conversational and voice-agent use. It offers four built-in voices (Sarah and Megan, female English speakers with UK and US accents; Theo and Jack, male English speakers with UK and US accents) and is English-only today, with Speechmatics saying more languages are planned. Speechmatics states the first audio chunk typically returns in under 200ms, with later chunks generated faster than real time, and output can be streamed as it is generated rather than waiting for the full response. The service launched as a free preview and has since moved onto Speechmatics' standard paid pricing tiers.
disadvantages: English only; Speechmatics says more languages are "coming soon" without a published date.
Only four fixed built-in voices (Sarah, Megan, Theo, Jack) are offered; there is no voice cloning.
No manual emotion, pitch or style controls; Speechmatics' own FAQ says fine-grained voice control "may be added in future releases."

together_ai/06_embedding_models.description: Together AI offers a suite of high-quality embedding models for transforming text into numerical vectors, supporting applications like search systems, recommendation engines, and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). together_ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7.description: MiniMax-M2.7 is MiniMax's 229-billion-parameter text model built for software engineering and long-horizon agentic work, including multi-agent collaboration and tool use through external scaffolding. MiniMax describes it as its first model to have deeply participated in its own development, running over 100 autonomous optimization rounds during training that it says produced a 30% improvement on internal programming benchmarks. It also targets office-productivity editing (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and reports strong identity and emotional-intelligence consistency for character-driven applications. MiniMax has since released MiniMax M3 as its newer flagship text model, though M2.7 remains generally available alongside it.
disadvantages: Superseded as MiniMax's flagship text model by MiniMax M3, which MiniMax's site lists as its newer, top-tier coding and multimodal model.

together_ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.description: MiniMax-M3 is MiniMax's natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts flagship model, released in June 2026, with roughly 428 billion total parameters and about 23 billion activated per token across 128 routed experts. MiniMax trained it on text and images together from the start rather than adding vision later, and built it around a new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) mechanism for long-context efficiency, natively supporting up to about 1,048,576 tokens. It offers a toggleable reasoning ('thinking') mode and is aimed at coding, long-horizon agentic tool use, and multimodal understanding, and is currently MiniMax's newest and most prominently featured text/multimodal model.
disadvantages: Bud's hosted providers serve roughly 512K tokens of context for this model, well below the ~1,048,576-token native context MiniMax describes, per MiniMax's GitHub card and Together AI's listing.
Released only a few months before this write-up (June 2026), so independent, longer-term evaluation is limited.

advantages: PrismML reports the model retains about 95% of the FP16 baseline's quality (80.49 vs. 85.07 average across 15 thinking-mode benchmarks) at roughly 1.71 bits per weight, about 9.4x smaller than FP16, per PrismML's Hugging Face model card.

Released under the Apache 2.0 license, per PrismML's Hugging Face model card.
together_ai/Prism-ML/Ternary-Bonsai-27B.description: Ternary Bonsai 27B is PrismML's ternary (three-value, ~1.71-bit-per-weight) quantization of Alibaba's Qwen3.6-27B, compressing the model roughly 9.4x versus its FP16 baseline. PrismML's own benchmark table reports it retains about 95% of full-precision quality, an 80.49 average across 15 thinking-mode benchmarks versus an 85.07 FP16 baseline. The compression runs end-to-end across embeddings, attention and MLP projections, and the LM head, leaving the base model's hybrid-attention architecture and 262,144-token context window unchanged, and PrismML releases it under the Apache 2.0 license. It is offered free through Together AI's serverless API.
disadvantages: A compressed, ternary-weight build of Qwen3.6-27B rather than a full-precision model; PrismML's own benchmark table shows a real, if small, quality gap versus its FP16 baseline (80.49 vs. 85.07 average across 15 thinking-mode benchmarks).

PrismML's own site presents a newer 'Bonsai 2 27B' model, built on Qwen3.8 27B with higher (98.2%) precision retention, as its most capable model, positioning this Qwen3.6-based 27B release as an earlier generation in the Bonsai family.

together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B.description: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, with 2.4 trillion total parameters and 95 billion activated per token across 512 experts (10 routed plus 1 shared), per its Hugging Face model card. together_ai/together/Tev1-4B-experimenta.description: Tev1-4B-experimental is Together AI's experimental decision-classifier model, a supervised fine-tune of Alibaba's Qwen3.5-4B built to select exactly one option from a structured state, question, and list of 2 to 24 labeled choices, returning only that option's letter. On Together's own development evaluation the model chose the correct option in 880 of 1,000 cases (88.0%) on its main decision set and 300 of 300 (100%) on a synthetic policy-transfer set, though Together's card states these are development results, not an independent benchmark, and that no untuned-Qwen baseline exists yet for comparison.

xai/grok-imagine-image-quality-20260403.description: grok-imagine-image-quality is one of three image models xAI offers in its Grok Imagine image family, also reachable under the aliases grok-imagine-image-quality-20260403, grok-imagine-image-quality-latest and grok-imagine-image-pro. Per xAI's own model documentation, it is a text-to-image generation system that also accepts an image input, so it can generate new images from a prompt or edit a supplied image from a natural-language description. xAI's own model-selection guide recommends its sibling model, grok-imagine-image-2.0, rather than this quality tier, as the default choice for image generation tasks. xAI has scheduled this model for retirement on November 2, 2026, after which requests to it will automatically be served by grok-imagine-image-2.0 at low quality, per xAI's migration guide.
disadvantages: xAI's own model-selection guide recommends grok-imagine-image-2.0 rather than this quality tier as the default model for image generation, per docs.x.ai.
Does not support xAI's Batch API, unlike the grok-imagine-image-2.0 model, per xAI's model documentation.
Rate-limited to 6 requests per second, per xAI's model documentation.

xai/grok-vision-beta.description: Grok Vision Beta is xAI's early-stage multimodal model introduced on November 19, 2024, offering basic vision capabilities for prototyping and experimentation. It supports image and text processing with an 8,192-token context window, handles JPG/PNG formats up to 10MB, and provides OCR and general visual analysis. Designed as a beta testing tier, it prioritizes accessibility for developers and researchers.
disadvantages: Limited to 8,192-token context window (1/4 of Grok-2 Vision's capacity)
Higher per-token costs compared to production models (2.5x input, 1.5x output)
Beta-level accuracy and reliability unsuitable for production workloads
Restricted to basic vision tasks with limited performance on complex documents or high-resolution analysis
Rate-limited to 1 request/second and 60 requests/hour for beta tier
use_cases: Prototyping multimodal applications and proof-of-concept development
Basic image description, captioning, and object identification
Simple text extraction from images (OCR) for non-critical workflows
Educational and research projects requiring accessible vision AI testing

xai/grok-voice-transcribe-1.0.description: grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 is a speech-to-text model in xAI's Grok Voice API, offered alongside a newer version, grok-voice-transcribe-2.0. It converts audio to text either through a single REST call or over a WebSocket stream, and xAI's API reference documents support for 12 audio formats, word-level timestamps, multichannel audio, speaker diarization, and Smart Turn end-of-turn detection, across 25 languages. xAI's docs set grok-voice-transcribe-2.0, not this version, as the default model for its Speech to Text endpoints.
disadvantages: xAI's documentation does not publish a word error rate or other accuracy benchmark for this model.
xAI's docs designate grok-voice-transcribe-2.0, not this version, as the default Speech to Text model.
use_cases: Batch transcription of recorded audio files or URLs.
Real-time transcription of streaming audio over WebSocket.
Multi-speaker call or meeting transcription with diarization and per-speaker word timestamps.
Voice-agent turn-taking, using Smart Turn end-of-turn detection to identify when a speaker has finished.

Multi-reference editing combines up to 5 input images in a single generation for compositing subjects, transferring styles, or composing scenes (xAI Imagine Image 2.0 launch post; xAI image-editing docs).
Plans typography and layout so dense, multi-part visuals hold together and small text renders sharply, per xAI (Imagine Image 2.0 launch post).
Generates images at resolutions up to 2K, with low, medium, and automatic quality tiers (xAI model registry, docs.x.ai).

xai/low/1024-x-1024/grok-imagine-image-2.description: Grok Imagine Image 2.0 is xAI's current text-to-image and image-editing model, launched August 7, 2026 as xAI's recommended image model. It serves as the 'Quality Mode' on grok.com/imagine and xAI's iOS/Android apps, and is available via the API as grok-imagine-image-2.0 (POST /v1/images/generations). It generates images at 1K, 1.5K, or 2K resolution with low, medium, or automatically-selected quality, and xAI says it 'follows instructions closely, down to the details,' planning typography and layout so dense, multi-part visuals hold together and small text renders sharply. Editing tools include region-targeted ('magic wand') edits, segmentation-based area selection, background removal to a transparent layer, multi-reference editing that combines up to 5 input images in one generation, and a 'smart resize' that refits an image to a new aspect ratio.
disadvantages: Image output only; xAI serves video generation as separate models (grok-imagine-video, grok-imagine-video-1.5).
use_cases: Photo editing and touch-ups via region-targeted edits and background removal
Product shots, headshots, icons, and game-asset generation using xAI's ready-made templates
Poster, packaging, and other typography-heavy graphic design where small text must stay legible
Multi-image compositing that combines subjects, styles, or props from up to 5 reference images
General text-to-image generation via the xAI API, grok.com/imagine, or xAI's iOS/Android apps
